title: Branch/merge safety for generated files: regenerate-in-CI, never merge
description: ODOC-231 Decision §4. Generated files are regenerated, never merged. .gitattributes (committed): generated files carry -merge linguist-generated=true, so a merge with conflicting generated content stops and declares a conflict rather than silently producing a plausible wrong file. The correctness gate is CI, never a merge driver (drivers live in uncommitted git config and forges do not run them) - a required check regenerates on the merge result and fails on git diff --exit-code; this fleet's exposure is PR merges into dev, since promotion is a fast-forward push and never runs a server-side merge. Change generated formats so they do not collide: one self-contained line per record, sorted by stable id, no summary/count/total lines, no central metadata block (Cargo lock-file precedent). Written, tested determinism contract: fixed key order, sorted collections, stable sort key = record id, no timestamps/counts/host/path strings; add lore render --check-deterministic (renders twice with shuffled input order, byte-compares). Managed regions use HTML-comment markers with no content hash in the marker line (a hash would manufacture a conflict on the one line that must stay stable); lore check already asserts region content equals regenerated content per existing behavior - confirm it holds under this contract. docs/log.md (LCLI-474, already Done) is the load-bearing defect already fixed for the merge-not-replace symptom; per the ADR, once per-document history (LCLI-547) is derived from the index, log.md becomes a pure function of the index and the clone-depth workaround can retire on evidence.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Generated files carry -merge linguist-generated=true in committed .gitattributes
A required CI check regenerates on the merge result and fails on git diff --exit-code; no correctness gate depends on a local merge driver
lore render --check-deterministic exists and asserts byte-identical output across shuffled input order
Every generated format follows the one-line-per-record, sorted-by-stable-id, no-central-metadata-block contract
Once LCLI-547 lands, docs/log.md is re-derived as a pure function of the index and the clone-depth-dependent merge workaround is retired on recorded evidence
